data.organizations: I am a member of Iota Phi Theta Fraternity Inc. I was initiated in Fall 2019 through the Alpha Omega alumni chapter in Baltimore, Maryland.  During that time, I held the following positions: 2020-2021: Community service chair; 2022-2023: Secretary.
data.priorKnowledge: Before the informational, my knowledge was very limited. During the early stages of learning about Kappa Pi. I explored the website and connected with some of the current members. I learned that Kappa Pi is an organization created to provide a space that supports black and brown individuals who identify as LGBTQIA+. The organization goes beyond creating those spaces, focusing heavily on community impact and social change.
data.essay1: Kappa Pi cultivates leaders dedicated to service, advocacy, and mentorship, focusing on empowering black and brown LGBTQIA+ communities. This aligns with my personal journey in the work that I do in higher education. My goal is always to have a positive and meaningful impact on those who look like me.
data.essay2:
As an Assistant Director of Residence Life, I have the privilege of mentoring Resident Assistants and supporting hundreds of students during the most transformative years of their lives. I strive to lead with authenticity, compassion, and accountability by creating environments where students feel respected and supported.

Outside of managing residence halls, I intentionally invest in leadership development by coaching student leaders, facilitating educational programs, helping students navigate personal and academic challenges, and encouraging them to become advocates within their own communities. I currently oversee a group called “Brothers of the Village”.This group was created to be a safe space for BIPOC individuals regardless of their gender identity or sexual orientation. While the title says “Brother” the group is open to students of all genders. Spaces like these let students know they are seen and valued. I believe that representation matters, and I aim to demonstrate that leadership can be compassionate, inclusive, and rooted in service.
data.essay3:
Service has always been an important part of my leadership philosophy. Through my work in higher education, I have coordinated and supported numerous service initiatives that encourage students to engage with their communities while addressing important social issues. I have helped organize campus-wide service opportunities (MLK Day of Service), educational awareness programs (Resident assistant programming), and community-building events that promote inclusion (Greek Food Drive), wellness, and civic engagement. I believe community service extends beyond volunteer hours. Service to me means consistently using your skills, resources, and influence to improve the lives of others. 

One of my most memorable moments was overseeing Greek life and the impact that the food drive had on students on campus, as well as the local community. We were able to donate over 5,000 items, including food, feminine hygiene products, kids' clothing, etc. 

With my chapter, I lead the initiative for voter registration. Partnering with Baltimore Votes, we held a "party at the polls" event encouraging community members to not only get out and vote, but also to register on the spot to ensure their information was current.
data.essay4:
I work intentionally to create affirming environments where every individual feels respected, valued, and empowered to be their authentic self. Throughout my career in student affairs, I have advocated for inclusive programming, encouraged open conversations about identity and belonging, and supported initiatives that promote visibility and acceptance for LGBTQIA+ students. I currently live in rural Ohio where most of the population looks nothing like me. I intentionally go out of my way to introduce myself to the BIPOC students on campus so they are aware of who I am and the resource I provide. 

I recognize that representation and affirmation can significantly influence someone's confidence and sense of belonging. By listening without judgment, mentoring students from diverse backgrounds, and fostering spaces where everyone is welcomed, I have encouraged greater involvement and helped individuals recognize their value and leadership potential. I pride myself on always being a listening ear because I have first-hand experience knowing what it feels like to be the "outsider".
data.essay5:
I bring a combination of leadership experience, student advocacy, event planning, mentorship, and organizational development. I have had the opportunity to lead projects of various sizes at the university and community level. My work in Residence Life and my experience in my organization have strengthened my ability to build inclusive communities, lead diverse teams, resolve conflict, and continue to develop myself as a leader amongst leaders. 

I am also skilled at creating educational programs, facilitating difficult conversations, and bringing people together around a common purpose. I believe my dedication to servant leadership, my commitment to equity and inclusion, and my passion for empowering others would allow me to make meaningful contributions to Kappa Pi. I hope to not only learn from the organization but also help strengthen its mission by being mentored by current members of the organization, supporting community initiatives, and representing Kappa Pi with integrity, professionalism, and pride.
